newsitem.title: FINLAND: PM Lipponen says not worried by markka strength.
newsitem.headline: PM Lipponen says not worried by markka strength.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was quoted as saying he was not worried by the recent strengthening of the markka.
"The moves on the money markets don't give reason for any particular concern," Lipponen said in an interview in regional daily Kouvolan Sanomat on Sunday.
"I think that the external value of the markka will remain stable," Lipponen said.
Support by central banks in other European Union countries to help the Bank of Finland halt the advance of the markka would not be needed, he said.
"Support by other central banks is possible, in principle, but this is not such a situation," Lipponen said, but did not elaborate.
The newspaper said Lipponen declined to comment on by how much the markka could fluctuate around its 3.04 per mark central parity in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
Last week, some analysts still expected the Bank of Finland to try to keep the markka within a 2.25 percent fluctuation band from the mid-point. The bank has said no such band exists.
In early trade on Monday, DEM/FIM traded at 2.9600 per mark -- over 2.6 percent stronger than the central parity.
